title: Malformed UTF-8 after a byte order mark is an encoding error at the byte, and the mark is not counted
notes: The stream is a UTF-8 byte order mark, the two-byte character U+00E9, a colon, a space, the byte 0xFF (which never occurs in UTF-8) and a line break. A YAML stream must be valid text in one of the encodings of section 5.2, so the text is refused as an encoding error; the specification does not say where an error is reported, so the position is the kit rule: the first byte of the ill-formed sequence, with the column counting the characters decoded before it, and the byte order mark is not a character of the text. Three characters come before the byte, so it is at 1:4. A reader that counts the mark reports column 5, one that counts bytes reports 8, and one that decodes leniently and reports a syntax error, or accepts the text, fails.

provenance.reference: Written for the kit to fill a gap: no case fixed the position of an encoding error in a stream that starts with a byte order mark.
